title: Stochastic Interpolants: A Unifying Framework for Flows and Diffusions

nodes.text: Stochastic interpolants are a class of continuous-time stochastic processes that bridge any two arbitrary probability densities exactly in finite time, built by combining data from both densities with an additional latent Gaussian variable that flexibly shapes the bridge.
nodes.evidence: a broad class of continuous-time stochastic processes called 'stochastic interpolants' to bridge any two arbitrary probability density functions exactly in finite time

nodes.text: The framework unifies flow-based and diffusion-based generative methods: the same interpolant density can be realized by an ODE (probability flow) and by forward/backward SDEs with a tunable diffusion coefficient.
nodes.evidence: A class of generative models that unifies flow-based and diffusion-based methods is introduced

nodes.text: The interpolant's time-dependent density satisfies a first-order transport equation and a family of forward and backward Fokker-Planck equations with a diffusion coefficient that can be varied at will, yielding both deterministic and stochastic generative models.
nodes.evidence: its density ρ(t) satisfies a first-order transport equation (TE) as well as a family of forward and backward Fokker-Planck equations (FPEs) with tunable diffusion coefficients

nodes.text: The drift (velocity) and score coefficients are characterized as the unique minimizers of simple quadratic objective functions estimated from data; a new quadratic objective is introduced for the score of the interpolant density (plus a denoiser objective related to the score).
nodes.evidence: The drift coefficients entering these models are time-dependent velocity fields characterized as the unique minimizers of simple quadratic objective functions, one of which is a new objective for the score of the interpolant density

nodes.text: Regressing the drift for SDE-based models controls the likelihood, but for ODE-based (deterministic) models likelihood control is more stringent, requiring additional minimization of a Fisher divergence.
nodes.evidence: regressing the drift for SDE-based models controls the likelihood, but that regressing the drift alone is not sufficient for ODE-based models, which must also minimize a Fisher divergence

nodes.text: Stochastic interpolants recover the Schrodinger bridge between the two target densities when explicitly optimizing over the interpolant.
nodes.evidence: we demonstrate that stochastic interpolants recover the Schrödinger bridge between the two target densities when explicitly optimizing over the interpolant

nodes.text: Unlike score-based diffusion models (SBDM) that map to a Gaussian via an OU process and take infinite time in both directions (requiring truncation), stochastic interpolants bridge two arbitrary densities exactly on a finite time interval without requiring one to be Gaussian.
nodes.evidence: the mapping takes infinite time in both directions, and hence must be truncated in practice... bridge two arbitrary densities... on a finite time interval

nodes.text: Score-based diffusion models can be re-written as one-sided stochastic interpolants after a time reparameterization, an approach that eliminates the singularities arising when naively compressing SBDM onto a finite-time interval.
nodes.evidence: score-based diffusion models can be re-written as one-sided interpolants after a reparameterization of time; we highlight how this approach eliminates singularities

nodes.text: Interpolants are equivalent to a class of stochastic bridges but avoid the need for Doob's h-transform, which is generically unknown, simplifying construction of a broad class of generative models.
nodes.evidence: interpolants are equivalent to a class of stochastic bridges, but that they avoid the need for Doob's h-transform, which is generically unknown

nodes.text: The rectification procedure applied to a learned generative model does not change the underlying generative model, though it may change the time-dependent density of the interpolant.
nodes.evidence: the rectification procedure does not change the underlying generative model, though it may change the time-dependent density of the interpolant

nodes.text: The approach learns the drift without simulation of the dynamics (simulation-free training) and can be deployed at sample-generation time through either deterministic or stochastic transport.
nodes.evidence: our approach allows us to learn the drift without simulation of the dynamics, and can be formulated at sample generation time through either deterministic or stochastic transport

nodes.text: Likelihood and cross-entropy estimators are derived for SDE-based interpolant generative models, serving as a counterpart to the continuous change-of-variables formula used for ODE-based likelihoods, and the approach is demonstrated on 2D, 128D Gaussian mixtures, and image generation.
nodes.evidence: we develop a general formula to evaluate the likelihood of SDE-based generative models that serves as a natural counterpart to the continuous change-of-variables formula

nodes.text: It remains an open question of significant practical importance whether there is a separation in sample quality between generative models based on deterministic versus stochastic dynamics; the framework is built to study this by sharing velocity and score estimates across ODE and SDE.
nodes.evidence: It is an open question of significant practical importance to understand if there exists a separation in sample quality between generative models based on deterministic dynamics and those based on stochastic dynamics
